title: Capacity fence: graded-decline modes for tenant-aware load shedding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight "capacity fence" admission layer that enforces per-tenant capacity budgets and exposes graded decline modes (soft-decline, trimmed-response, delayed-exec) to reduce blast radius during spikes and multi-region failover. This ticket covers prototyping the fence, integrating with circuit-breaker state, and adding telemetry for SLO/quality tracking.

Motivation: current emergency shedding is all-or-nothing or relies on coarse token-buckets which causes sharp quality cliffs for high-traffic tenants. The capacity fence aims to: 1) honor tenant budgets and SLO classes; 2) degrade responses gracefully rather than drop; 3) interoperate with regional failover so tenants using standby regions get predictable degraded behavior instead of opaque timeouts.

Scope:
- Admission layer that computes an active budget score per request (tenant, route, model)
- Three graded decline modes: soft-decline (reduce non-essential features, e.g., n-best expansions), trimmed-response (token truncation + compressed payloads), delayed-exec (queue with max wait + fallback to partial response)
- Tie fence state to circuit-breaker signals (open/half-open => increase decline level)
- Operator API to set tenant fence policies and emergency override
- Metrics and SLO impact dashboard: 95th/99th latency, success rate, perceived-quality regression by prompt-suite, per-tenant degraded-response rate

Non-goals: full rewrite of existing token-bucket implementation, long-term autoscaling changes (separate project).

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We prefer soft degraded outputs over synthetic errors for customer experience, but this adds complexity in model prompts (must support structured metadata to indicate trimming).
- Tight coupling between fence and model-level trimming requires small compatibility shim in the runtime to accept 'decline-hints' on requests.
- We choose a staged rollout: internal traffic -> P0 tenants -> region canary -> global. Fallback policy will revert to best-effort token-bucket when fence fails.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype integrated in runtime can apply decline modes per tenant without schema-breaking API changes
- Dashboards show per-tenant degradation metrics and no SLO regressions for P0 tenants in canary window
- Automated chaos test (regional failover) demonstrates system maintains availability with graceful degraded responses rather than timeouts for 90% of traffic

Metrics to track:
- Degraded-response-rate (by decline mode)
- Tokens emitted per request pre/post decline
- User-facing error rate and median latency
- Quality delta on benchmark prompts (expected <= 15% quality loss for trimmed-response mode)

Rollout plan:
1) Dev prototype behind feature flag (runtime + gateway) on internal cluster (2 weeks)
2) Canary on internal paid customers (1 week)
3) P0 tenant alpha with opt-in and strict monitoring (2 weeks)
4) Gradual region canary during low-traffic window, with automatic rollback if degradation > thresholds.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: model clients misinterpret trimmed responses. Mitigation: add structured response metadata and update SDKs to surface that info.
- Risk: increased operator complexity. Mitigation: provide sensible defaults and a single-page operator console for fence status and override.
